title: Histogram-driven mini-batch shaper for sequence-length variance
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a histogram-driven micro-batch shaper that reduces wasted padding across prefill and decode phases by creating compact mini-batches (slots) from request length distributions and aligning kernel selection decisions with those slots.
background: Current continuous-batching packs requests into buckets using coarse length bins which leaves >12% token overhead for many corpora (chat + docs mixed workloads). This overhead increases token compute and memory pressure, and triggers suboptimal kernel paths for short vs long sequences. Existing experiments (ENG-4721, ENG-62045) show gains from seqlen-aware coalescing but do not tie scheduling to kernel heuristics or prefill/decode split optimizations.
proposed_solution: Build a lightweight on-request histogram collector (per-worker, time-decayed) to produce micro-batch slots: 1) compute a compact length histogram (quantized) for recent incoming requests, 2) derive mini-batch shapes that minimize sum(padding*batch_size) subject to latency SLOs, 3) schedule prefill and decode separately so prefill uses packing aggressive coalescing while decode prefers low-latency interleaving. The scheduler will expose a small scoring API to the kernel selector so we can prefer fused/fast-kernel variants for slots with uniform lengths.
implementation_steps: Add telemetry: per-worker seqlen histogram (exponentially decaying window, 1s granularity) and expose an API to sample histograms.
Implement shape solver: greedy bin merge with constraint on max queuing time (configurable per-customer SLO), output mini-batch shapes and per-slot priority.
Integrate scheduler into request dispatcher: create slots, assign requests to slots, mark prefill vs decode reservation, and emit packing plans to runtime.
Extend kernel selector: provide slot metadata (avg_len, variance) and add heuristic to pick kernels optimized for homogenous spans (use smaller-kernel fast paths when variance < threshold).
KV-cache alignment: ensure packed prefill maintains contiguous KV layout; add compact KV writes for merged short-seq slots.
Add feature flag gated rollout and AB experiment to compare against baseline bucketing with telemetry hooks.
Performance tests and resource limits: add guard rails when slot packing would exceed GPU mem or throughput targets.
testing_plan: Unit tests for histogram collector and solver determinism
Microbench harness: synthetic workloads (chat-heavy, doc-heavy, mixed) comparing avg padding, GPU token/s, latency p50/p95, and memory use
End-to-end staging run with traffic shadowing for 48h to validate stability and regression detection
Canary rollout on 10% of traffic with automatic rollback if token-efficiency regression or latency SLO breach occurs
rollout_strategy: Feature-flagged canary -> 10% -> 30% -> 100% with observability gates. Gate conditions: token-efficiency improvement >= 4% without p95 latency regression > 5% or OOMs. Rollback automated via console runbook if gates fail.
success_metrics: tokens_per_second_increase: target >= 2% under common customer traces
risks_mitigation: Risk: Overpacking increases p95 due to head-of-line blocking. Mitigation: max_queue_time parameter and reserve decode-priority slots to bypass heavy packing.
Risk: Kernel selection mismatch could pick slow kernels for edge cases. Mitigation: conservative kernel-hint thresholds and fallbacks to baseline kernel if slot execution is slower than expected.
Risk: KV cache fragmentation when merging different-length prefill. Mitigation: compact KV write path and GC heuristics plus mem-safety checks.
Risk: Telemetry overhead. Mitigation: histogram uses compact sketch (fixed 32 bins) and sampling rate control.
Risk: Variation across GPU topologies. Mitigation: profile-run per-topology and tune solver cost model for each target fleet.
notes: Design favors a low-latency path for decode traffic; prefill can accept slightly higher queuing to save GPU cost. The solver is intentionally greedy to keep CPU overhead minimal. We'll expose customer-configurable knobs for max_queue_time and bin_count.
